rationales: Prophase is when chromosomes condense, not align at the equator.
Metaphase is when chromosomes line up along the cell’s equator.
Anaphase is when sister chromatids move toward opposite poles.
Telophase is when new nuclei form around the separated chromosomes.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives, not a group of organisms.
The biosphere includes all regions of Earth where life exists.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
A population consists of members of the same species living in the same place at the same time.
Hydrogen makes up about 10 percent of protoplasm.
Eighteen percent is approximately the proportion of carbon in protoplasm.
Sixty-five percent is approximately the proportion of oxygen in protoplasm.
Three percent is approximately the proportion of nitrogen in protoplasm.
1880 is not the year associated with A. F. A. King’s observations about malaria.
A. F. A. King listed 20 observations about malaria in 1883.
1878 is not the year associated with A. F. A. King’s observations about malaria.
1898 is not the year associated with A. F. A. King’s observations about malaria.
A phylum is a higher taxonomic rank than a group of related families.
An order is the taxonomic rank comprising related families.
A class comprises related orders, not families directly.
A genus comprises related species, not families.
Collenchyma consists of elongated cells with unevenly thickened primary walls.
Sclerenchyma has thick, usually lignified secondary walls rather than unevenly thickened primary walls.
Parenchyma cells generally have thin primary walls.
Epidermal tissue forms a protective covering and is not characterized by these wall thickenings.
Lipids are mainly synthesized in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Ribosomes attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesize proteins.
Carbohydrates are not the main products synthesized by rough endoplasmic reticulum.
DNA is replicated in the nucleus, not synthesized by rough endoplasmic reticulum.
In prophase, chromosomes condense but chromatids remain joined.
In metaphase, chromosomes align at the equator while chromatids remain joined.
In anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.
In telophase, separated chromosomes are enclosed in newly forming nuclei.
Fifty to seventy thousand is far below the approximate daily cell death count.
Fifty to seventy lakh is also far below the approximate daily cell death count.
Fifty to seventy million is below the approximate daily cell death count.
About 50–70 billion cells die by apoptosis each day in an adult human.
Leukaemia is a cancer of blood-forming tissues, not the death of heart tissue.
Arteriosclerosis is the hardening and thickening of arteries.
Myocardial infarction is the death of heart muscle tissue due to interrupted blood supply.
Thalassaemia is an inherited disorder affecting haemoglobin production.
Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the red and blue regions of the spectrum.
Chlorophyll reflects much of the green light, so it does not absorb it maximally.
Green and red is incorrect because green is not a region of maximum chlorophyll absorption.
Green and blue is incorrect because chlorophyll also absorbs strongly in red, not green.
Enzymes are generally proteins, not carbohydrates.
Lipids are not the general molecular category to which enzymes belong.
Nucleic acids store and transmit genetic information rather than forming the usual enzyme category.
Most enzymes are proteins that catalyse biochemical reactions.
Ibn-e-Nafees is credited in the textbook with first presenting the concept of metabolism.
Wilhelm Kühne is associated with defining enzymes, not first giving the concept of metabolism.
Emil Fischer is known for work on enzyme specificity and the lock-and-key model.
Jabir Bin Hayan is not credited with first presenting the concept of metabolism.
Metaphase is when spindle fibres are attached to chromosomes and aligned at the equator.
G2 phase is part of interphase and precedes mitosis, when the mitotic spindle is not formed.
Spindle fibres begin to form during prophase.
Interphase is the period of growth and DNA replication before mitosis.
Species is the basic unit of biological classification.
Genus is a taxonomic rank containing related species.
Family is a higher rank containing related genera.
Class is a higher rank containing related orders.
